## Top project memories
- [MEM003] (pattern) Editorial shell uses CSS custom properties as the canonical token layer (--color-paper, --color-ink, --color-oxblood, etc.) with Tailwind referencing them via var() — keeps runtime theming possible and avoids Tailwind JIT purge issues with dynamic class names. Components use inline styles bound to tokens rather than Tailwind utility classes.
- [MEM004] (gotcha) CRA's pinned @testing-library/react emits a ReactDOMTestUtils.act() deprecation warning on React 18 — this is a console warning, not a test failure. Resolving it would require ejecting or overriding CRA's dependency resolution to upgrade @testing-library/react to 14+. Safe to ignore for now.
- [MEM005] (convention) The editorial shell test at src/__tests__/editorial-shell.test.js includes a source-file read assertion (fs.readFileSync) to detect re-introduction of legacy imports (MatrixRain, cosmic, terminal components). This gives future agents a deterministic, browser-free signal for regression detection.
- [MEM001] (architecture) Portfolio redesign visual direction Chose: One-page editorial scroll with Spectral-first Plantin-like typography, warm cream paper background, restrained ink/oxblood palette, and long-form novel pacing.. Rationale: The user wants LaTeX/novel seriousness combined with Zara/Apple/pi.dev-level smoothness; a text-first editorial system fits that better than card grids, cosmic graphics, or terminal aesthetics..
- [MEM002] (architecture) GitHub activity data architecture Chose: Fetch GitHub activity at build time into static JSON, then render from that artifact in React.. Rationale: Build-time fetch avoids client-side token exposure, lowers rate-limit risk, keeps the static GitHub Pages deployment fast, and still supports nightly refresh via GitHub Actions later..

# T01: Added a safe build-time GitHub REST fetch script and npm command that writes sanitized activity data to src/data/githubActivity.json with graceful fallback support.

**Added a safe build-time GitHub REST fetch script and npm command that writes sanitized activity data to src/data/githubActivity.json with graceful fallback support.**

## What Happened

Created scripts/fetch-github-activity.js as a CommonJS Node CLI that reads .env directly without printing values, resolves GITHUB_TOKEN_PORTFOLIO before GITHUB_TOKEN, requests the aatif101 profile, repos, and public events through GitHub REST, aggregates public signals, sanitizes repository and event payloads, and writes the static JSON artifact consumed by the app. Added src/data/githubActivity.json as the static output artifact and wired package.json with npm run fetch-github-activity. Added Jest coverage for dotenv parsing/token precedence, Authorization header containment, sanitized activity shaping, and fallback output shape. The script logs only non-secret phases, endpoint classes, status/rate-limit metadata, fallback state, and output path.

## Verification

Ran focused Jest tests via gsd_exec node/cmd.exe because bash is unavailable in this Windows runner. Ran npm run fetch-github-activity, which successfully queried GitHub REST and wrote src/data/githubActivity.json with fallback=false. Ran an additional artifact/log safety validation that parsed the generated JSON and scanned captured fetch output for Authorization, Bearer token patterns, or GITHUB_TOKEN markers; no leakage was found.

## Verification Evidence

| # | Command | Exit Code | Verdict | Duration |
|---|---------|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | `npm test -- --watchAll=false --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/github-activity-fetch.test.js` | 0 | ✅ pass | 4944ms |
| 2 | `npm run fetch-github-activity` | 0 | ✅ pass | 1502ms |

# T03: Rendered a wide editorial GitHub activity spread from the static artifact and integrated it into the homepage with fallback visibility.

**Rendered a wide editorial GitHub activity spread from the static artifact and integrated it into the homepage with fallback visibility.**

## What Happened

Added `GitHubActivity` as an editorial annual-report style spread that imports the static GitHub activity artifact, computes a large headline metric, renders a cream/oxblood contribution-style data print, lists recent public activity, lists active repositories, and shows a tally/status line. Integrated the spread into `EditorialPortfolio` as a wide `#github-activity` section with navigation. The component renders explicit fallback labels and fallback empty-state copy when the artifact is marked as fallback or lacks activity/repositories, so missing/stale fetch data remains visible without crashing. Added a regression assertion in the editorial shell test to confirm the homepage exposes the new activity report, headings, and status label.

## Verification

Ran the production CRA build successfully. Also ran the editorial shell regression test after adding the GitHub spread assertion; all 10 shell tests passed.
